gaps.text: In-line measurement of Resin temperature with temperature sensor at the probe location

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: MIR-ATR and Raman spectra from the same probe spot merged into one matrix after synchronisation to a common time step and block scaling. Each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches, otherwise the extra instrument is dropped.)
Direct in-line optical measurement of viscosity, or spectroscopy of curing resins specifically, is not covered by the supplied material.
No source gives an achievable MIR fiber link length for a vessel installation.

items.finding: The effectiveness of multi-sensor fusion does not increase proportionally with the number of sensors; rather, it hinges on mutual correction and complementarity among different sensors.
items.how_it_applies: Before implementing data fusion of MIR-ATR and Raman, evaluate whether both modalities offer genuine complementarity for monitoring the curing resin.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study evaluated optical responses in food matrices rather than reactive resins inside a heated vessel, so performance gains may not transfer directly.

citation.quote: It is noteworthy that the effectiveness of multi-sensor fusion does not increase proportionally with the number of sensors; rather, it hinges on mutual correction and complementarity among different sensors.
